transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As we get into our weekly planning meeting, I'd like to put the P-7 gearbox maintenance on the table for discussion this weekend. I'll be making the final call on the maintenance window and operating plan, but I want to hear from maintenance, logistics, and safety before we lock anything in. A few things we'll need to work through: P-7 normally transfers finished pallets to Dock 3, and we've got limited space for manually staged pallets in the finished-goods area, so we need a solid plan for how to handle throughput while the palletizer is down. Let's start with maintenance — what's the scope of the gearbox work and how long do you expect the palletizer to be offline?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share what I found in my vibration assessment yesterday. I discovered a cracked gearbox bearing in P-7 that could seize under load. My strong recommendation is to start the replacement this Saturday at 06:00. The work will take exactly 6 hours, and critically, P-7 must not operate at all during the repair. I completed the assessment yesterday but haven't yet attached it to the maintenance work order — I'll make sure that gets done today.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something important for this plan. I received a carrier confirmation by email that I haven't entered on the shipping board yet: exactly 22 finished-goods pallets must be ready for Monday's 06:00 pickup. The good news is the carrier can collect them at Dock 1 instead of Dock 3 — but only if we book the reroute by Friday afternoon. Given that P-7 normally transfers to Dock 3 and we're taking it offline this weekend, we should factor this into the maintenance window and the staging plan.
